phase_title: HATP Prerequisite DAG Correction and Next Real-Effect Node Selection (HMIC Certification vs. FIDO2 Hardware-Credential Enrollment)
recommended_next_phase: The narrow real-effect phase corresponding only to 149O.20L.7O.2K's selected node -- HMIC CertificationRecord creation (create only, per 2K section 25's frozen envelope) -- not pre-named with a specific future phase ID by 2K itself. That phase must independently obtain Protected Admin Authority's fresh election and confirmation before invoking scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py create, and must re-run 2K's read-only prechecks fresh at its own entry rather than reusing 2K's tables uncritically. Not started, not authorized by 2K.
summary: Phase 149O.20L.7O.2K is an analysis/authorization-only phase that corrected 149O.20L.7O.2I's stale prerequisite DAG per 149O.20L.7O.2J's primary evidence (Protected Root already satisfies HBDC-REQ-011..018; a freshness recheck, not creation, is the only remaining Protected-Root-adjacent action), then independently selected exactly one next real-effect node between HMIC CertificationRecord creation and FIDO2 hardware-credential enrollment. Reading HMIC-001 v1.6, HBDC-001 v1.2, HPSE-001 v1.1, HHCE-001, and production source directly (not from phase-history summary), this phase found that HMIC's 12-step validation algorithm never reads hardware-credentials.json, registry.json principal/signer sections, or deployment-bindings.json -- certification attests source identity, contract identity, and repository/deployment identity only, never trust-record content; the source code implementing hardware-credential and principal/signer enrollment IS bound into HMIC's 36-member frozen identity, but the runtime data those modules write is not, so a future FIDO2 enrollment cannot invalidate an existing certification's implementation_scope_digest. Class-B deployment validity and HMIC certification were confirmed to be independent sibling readiness terms inside HMRC-001's six-item conjunction, not sequential dependents, and no cycle was found when re-testing the specific candidate cycle the governing prompt named. FIDO2 enrollment was found blocked today on two independent, evidence-based gaps: no physical FIDO2/PIV device is confirmed present on hac-dell (last primary evidence, 149O.20L.7O.2C, found one ABSENT, and this analysis-only phase performed no SSH to refresh that fact), and no standalone scripts/hatp_hardware_credential_admin.py or scripts/hatp_principal_signer_admin.py admin-script entrypoint exists in this repository, unlike HMIC certification and DeploymentBinding creation, which each already have a real, frozen, standalone scripts/ admin tool. HMIC certification, by contrast, has zero unmet predecessor today. This phase therefore selected HMIC CertificationRecord creation (the create-only ceremony, explicitly excluding the separate activate ceremony) as the next real-effect node, explicitly rejected FIDO2 enrollment for this cycle on unmet-predecessor grounds rather than contract disfavor, and froze a narrow authorization envelope for a future, separate real-effect phase (exact admin ceremony scripts/hatp_certification_admin.py create, exact prechecks reusing 2J's frozen read-only envelope, exact record written, exact post-write validation expecting the readiness-affecting active binding to remain MISSING, exact failure/rollback/idempotency behavior) -- not executed by this phase. A 21-test focused evidence suite passed. Fast_green git-stash differential comparison showed zero attributable regressions: 326 failed/8174 passed/7 skipped/9 errors on the pre-phase baseline versus 326 failed/8195 passed/7 skipped/9 errors with this phase's changes, a delta of exactly the 21 new passing tests this phase added. HMIC-001 v1.6 (36 source-identity members, 7 contract_versions members) and HBDC-001 v1.2 remain byte-unchanged; no production src/pcae source was modified by this phase.
